builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training
summary: The method replaces naive early-stopping rules (pruning by current accuracy) in population-based training with learned predictors that forecast final test accuracy from checkpoint features (weight statistics, SANE latent tokens), terminating low-ranked candidates early. It costs training an auxiliary nowcaster (and optionally a transformer autoencoder for SANE embeddings) plus periodic checkpoint analysis, and in homogeneous zoos it adds little over the free baseline of pruning by current accuracy. It can fail when the nowcaster is trained on a model zoo unrepresentative of the reader's architectures or hyperparameter distribution, when learning curves cross in ways the predictor misses, and it presupposes budget to train multiple candidates in parallel.
rationale: The reader with one 24 GB GPU may run modest hyperparameter populations where predicted-pruning could save compute, but the benefit is validated only on specific model zoos and the predictor requires training on representative prior runs, so workload-specific validation is required before adoption.
technique: Nowcast-based population pruning in hyperparameter search

claims.statement: The method replaces naive early-stopping rules (pruning by current accuracy) in population-based training with learned predictors that forecast final test accuracy from checkpoint features (weight statistics, SANE latent tokens), terminating low-ranked candidates early. It costs training an auxiliary nowcaster (and optionally a transformer autoencoder for SANE embeddings) plus periodic checkpoint analysis, and in homogeneous zoos it adds little over the free baseline of pruning by current accuracy. It can fail when the nowcaster is trained on a model zoo unrepresentative of the reader's architectures or hyperparameter distribution, when learning curves cross in ways the predictor misses, and it presupposes budget to train multiple candidates in parallel.

In heterogeneous model zoos (ResNet-18, ViT), SOTF with nowcasted final accuracy nearly closes the gap to the best model compared to pruning by current accuracy; no speedup or cost factor is quantified.
